Administering KoldFusion Server

Java

New in KoldFusion 4.5. The Java page configures the Java Virtual Machine that runs CFOBJECT TYPE="Java" and CreateObject("Java", ...), Java CFX tags and CFSERVLET, and shows whether it is running.

Go there: Open the Java page (or inside the frameset)

Java Virtual Machine status

The box at the top of the page tells you where things stand:

  • Not loaded: a JVM was found (the page shows which libjvm.so, and how it was found). KoldFusion starts it the first time a page uses Java. Click Load JVM to start it now.
  • Loaded: the Java version, the library, when it started, how much of the heap is in use, how many request threads are attached and how many Java objects CFML variables are holding, plus the class path and the exact options it was started with.
  • No Java Virtual Machine found: install a JDK or JRE, or enter the path below. Everything that does not use Java keeps working; Java features report an error of type Object.
  • Failed: the JVM refused to start with these options. Correct them and restart the server.

A second line checks for cfx.jar, which Java CFX tags and CFSERVLET need (CFOBJECT does not).

Settings

Field Default Purpose
Java Virtual Machine Path (blank) The JVM library (libjvm.so), or a JDK/JRE directory containing one. Blank: look in JAVA_HOME, for java on the PATH, in /usr/lib/jvm/* and in ~/.local/jdk/*
Class Path (blank) Extra directories and JAR files, separated by semicolons. cfx.jar and kfroot/java/classes are always on the class path
Initial Heap Size 4096 KB Starting heap
Max Heap Size 65536 KB Largest heap
System Options (blank) Java system properties, as OPT1=value;OPT2=value (each becomes -DOPT1=value)
Implementation Options (blank) Other JVM options, such as -Xss512k;-XX:+UseSerialGC
CFX Jar Path kfroot/java/cfx.jar The cfx.jar with the Java CFX and servlet interfaces

Click Apply to save. A process can start only one JVM, so once it is loaded, changes take effect when the server is restarted.

Notes

  • make builds cfx.jar and the sample classes when it finds javac. Without a JDK the server still builds and runs; only the Java features are unavailable.
  • Classes, Java CFX tags and servlets placed in kfroot/java/classes are found without touching the Class Path. CFX tags and servlets there are reloaded when their .class file changes.
  • KoldFusion always adds -Xrs (so Ctrl+C still stops the server), -Djava.awt.headless=true, and the system properties koldfusion.root and koldfusion.webroot; it uses the serial garbage collector unless the Implementation Options name another one.
  • Setting the environment variable KF_NOJVM=1 makes KoldFusion behave as if no JVM were installed.

Note  In 1999 a 16 MB heap was generous. Your workstation had 64 MB of RAM, and Netscape wanted most of it.
